title: Apple cider pork chops with roasted squash

items: 4 bone-in pork chops, about 1 inch thick
1 small butternut squash (about 2 lb), peeled, seeded and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 crisp apple (such as Honeycrisp), cored and sliced ¼ inch thick
2 Tbsp unsalted butter, cut into pieces
1 tsp fresh thyme leaves (or ½ tsp dried)

steps: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
Toss the squash with the oil, salt and cinnamon on the pan and spread it in a single layer. Roast 25–30 min, flipping once halfway, until fork-tender and browned at the edges.
While the squash roasts, pat the chops dry with paper towels and season both sides with the salt and pepper.

Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high heat until it shimmers. Sear the chops 4–5 min without moving them, until deep golden. Flip, lower the heat to medium and cook 4–6 min more, until they read 145°F in the thickest part away from the bone.
Move the chops to a plate, cover loosely with foil and rest 3 min. Pour off all but 1 Tbsp of the fat.

Add the apple slices to the skillet over medium heat and cook 2 min, until they start to soften. Add the cider, Dijon and brown sugar, scraping up the browned bits. Boil 5–7 min, until reduced by half and syrupy.
Take the pan off the heat and swirl in the butter and thyme until the sauce is glossy. Stir in any juices from the resting plate.
Spoon the apples and sauce over the chops and serve with the squash.
tips: Buy pre-cut butternut squash to save about 10 min of prep.
Thinner chops (½ inch) need only 2–3 min per side. Check the temperature early so they don't dry out.
storage: Fridge up to 3 days. Reheat the chops covered in a skillet over medium-low heat with a splash of cider or water so they stay moist. Reheat the squash in a 400°F oven 8–10 min.
